title: Validate BST Ordering
statement: You are given a binary tree encoded as a level-order array, where None marks a missing child (so children of absent nodes are omitted). Return True if the tree is a valid binary search tree and False otherwise. A tree is a valid BST when, for every node, all values in its left subtree are strictly less than the node's value and all values in its right subtree are strictly greater than the node's value. Equal values are never allowed, so any duplicate value makes the tree invalid. An empty tree (empty array, or an array whose first element is None) is valid and returns True.
hints: It is not enough to check each node against only its own two children -- a node deep in a subtree can still violate an ancestor's ordering. What range of values is each node actually allowed to hold?

Recurse with an open interval (low, high) that every node in the current subtree must fall strictly inside; going left tightens the upper bound to the parent's value, going right tightens the lower bound.

Build the tree from the level-order array, then call check(node, low, high): return True at None; return False if not (low < node.val < high); otherwise return check(left, low, node.val) and check(right, node.val, high), starting at (-inf, +inf). Strict comparisons reject duplicates automatically.
